svg.title: One-step positive-log integrability propagates through a finite cocycle horizon
svg.desc: A central vertical path begins with an explicit one-step positive-log integrability assumption, pulls that observable back along every natural iterate of a measure-preserving base, adds finitely many shifted terms into an integrable orbit sum, and uses pointwise domination to conclude finite-horizon positive-log integrability. A side warning states that the positive-log gate already discarded exact collapse and contraction. The footer excludes probability, ergodicity, limits, and Lyapunov conclusions.
svg.text: Propagate one explicit integrability assumption through a finite horizon
Measure-preserving pullbacks, finite addition, and domination do separate jobs.
ONE-STEP POSITIVE-LOG NORM IS INTEGRABLE
an explicit hypothesis about the generator's expanding tail
ordinary real-valued integrability against the stated raw measure
INFORMATION WARNING
collapse was clipped to zero
contraction was clipped to zero
the envelope keeps expansion only
it is not the full log norm
PULL BACK ALONG EVERY NATURAL BASE ITERATE
each shifted one-step term remains integrable
measure preservation transports the assumption; it does not create it
ADD THE SHIFTED TERMS OVER ONE FINITE RANGE
the orbit-sum envelope is integrable by finite-sum closure
no independence, infinite series, or uniform time bound is used
DOMINATE THE FINITE-HORIZON POSITIVE LOG
nonnegativity removes the absolute value in the integrability bound
pointwise majorization is stronger than the required almost-everywhere bound
EVERY FIXED FINITE-HORIZON POSITIVE-LOG NORM IS INTEGRABLE
the conclusion remains finite-time and expansion-only
No probability normalization, ergodicity, negative-log control, normalized limit, or Lyapunov conclusion.
